question: What are the strongest arguments on both sides of McKesson, what are the probability-weighted 12-to-18 month outcomes, and what exact triggers govern our capital?

epigraph.quote: Conviction without a price discipline is just expensive stubbornness; price discipline without conviction misses the compounders.

web_blocks.title: Both Sides of the Aisle: Bull vs. Bear Steelman

book_paragraphs: Great investing comes down to holding two opposing ideas in your head at once and refusing to flinch from either. Before we lock in our final verdict on McKesson, let's put the strongest Bull case and the sharpest Bear case side by side.

The Bull steelman rests on structural transformation. McKesson sits at the center of a three-player drug distribution oligopoly controlling over 90% of U.S. volume [19]. Instead of standing still as a low-margin box-mover, management exited European retail and is separating its Wellverse Med-Surg unit with Apollo's $1.25 billion backing [9, 10]. Its FY2027E sources-and-uses bridge pairs $1.25 billion in Apollo Wellverse equity, $2.25 billion in Med-Surg term loan proceeds, and $5.4 billion to $6.0 billion in annual free cash flow (~$9.0 billion to $9.5 billion total sources) to fund the $2.25 billion Precision Medicine Group acquisition (closed November 2, 2026), the $1.40 billion proposed 49% Option Care Health stake, and $4.5 billion to $5.0 billion in annual buybacks—with buybacks able to moderate to $3.5 billion to $4.0 billion during integration to keep net leverage below 1.5x EBITDA [2, 9, 10, 12, 13]. Meanwhile, Oncology & Multispecialty hit a 2.96% margin (+53% profit growth) and RxTS earns nearly 20% margins [2]. At 20.4x forward earnings, McKesson is compounding faster than its multiple implies [25].

Now hear the Bear steelman without sugarcoating it. Core pharma distribution gross margin compressed to 3.6% as lower-margin GLP-1 sales surged [2, 20]. Customer concentration remains high: CVS Health is roughly 24% of sales, and the top ten customers are 73% [2]. On policy, IRA Medicare Part B drug negotiation and 340B rebate shifts could pinch specialty economics [4, 20]. The August 2026 cloud data incident also highlights rising cyber risk [16]. Add $5.06 billion in opioid liabilities, $2.56 billion in redeemable minority interests, and a stock stretched nearly 10% above its 50-day line in a Downtrend [2, 3, 21, 24]. Near-term drawdown risk is real.

Weighing both sides, we map three 18-to-24 month scenarios. In our Bull case (25% probability), PMG and Core Ventures synergies speed up, Wellverse separates cleanly, and MCK reaches $1,350.00 (+26.2% from today, or +40.3% from our $962.50 entry midpoint). In our Base case (55% probability), MCK reaches $1,200.00 (+12.2% from today, or +24.7% from $962.50), anchored to FY2029E adjusted EPS of ~$59.10 (+12.7% YoY from FY2028E $52.44) at a flat 20.3x forward P/E (equivalent to 22.9x FY2028E EPS). In our Bear case (20% probability), policy headwinds or a Downtrend de-rating pull the multiple to 16.5x stressed earnings, or $820.00 (-23.3% from today).

Multiply those probabilities together, and you get an expected value of $1,161.50 per share. From $1,069.43, that is only +8.6% expected upside—not enough to justify taking $211.74 of stop-loss risk down to $857.69. Yet from our $940.00–$985.00 pullback zone, the exact same business delivers +20.7% expected value and 1.69:1 support-zone asymmetry. That is why we override the raw quantitative screen's BUY_AT_CMP_NO_FOMO signal to ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP: 1W RSI (71.10) is overbought, the S&P 500 sits in a Downtrend (40.4% breadth >50DMA and 10 distribution days), and CMP reward-to-risk is just 0.62:1. Across our three horizons, the playbook is consistent. Wait on short-term momentum (1–3 months) while 1W RSI (71.10) cools. Accumulate on dips at $940–$985 for the 6-to-24 month Wellverse and PMG inflection. Hold as a Tier 1 Core Alpha compounder for 3-to-5+ years.

Finally, because we hold zero shares (NOT_HELD), we keep 100% of our earmarked capital in cash. We put 0% in shortlist alternative Eli Lilly (LLY) and 0% in outside peer Cencora (COR), letting price alerts bring McKesson to our $940.00–$985.00 shelf. If McKesson reaches our entry zone, our hard invalidation stop goes straight in at $857.69. We will also watch three falsifiable signposts: Oncology and RxTS margin durability, smooth Wellverse/PMG execution, and respect for the 30-week moving average floor.

Remember why those three signposts matter so much. First, if Oncology & Multispecialty holds above a 2.9% margin and RxTS holds near 19%+, our $52.44 FY2028 EPS model stays on track [2, 6]. Second, if Wellverse separates cleanly and PMG integrates without cash burn, net leverage stays well below 2.0x EBITDA [3, 9, 14]. Third, if price holds the $940–$985 shelf on light volume, the Stage 2 uptrend remains intact [24].

On the flip side, we have clear rules if the thesis breaks. A heavy-volume drop below $857.69 violates both the 30-week SMA ($870.67) and 200-day SMA ($879.78) [24]. If that happens while filled, we exit at the stop. If it happens before we enter, we cancel all open buy orders and re-underwrite from scratch.

book_subsections.title: Why Cash Is a Position: Rejecting Inferior Substitutes While Waiting
paragraphs: One of the hardest habits for active investors to master is refusing to force money into a second-best idea just because their first-choice stock is temporarily extended. When McKesson sits at $1,069.43, it is tempting to look around the healthcare sector and ask whether we should deploy that capital into Eli Lilly on our shortlist or Cencora as an outside peer instead. Our redeployment audit gives a clear answer: zero percent to both.

Eli Lilly is a world-class pharmaceutical innovator growing revenue at 45.51%, yet at $1,347.11 it trades at 44.26x trailing earnings with only 0.71:1 reward-to-risk to a $1,480 target against its $1,158.67 stop. Cencora trades at a lower 15.63x forward P/E, yet it carries 3.06x debt-to-equity and earns 23.63% ROIC—less than a third of McKesson's 76.71% ROIC [25, 26]. Neither substitute offers the combination of oligopoly durability, software-like RxTS margins, and clean balance-sheet flexibility that McKesson brings.

Keeping 100% of earmarked capital in cash while the S&P 500 works through a Downtrend is not passivity; it is active risk management. By setting limit alerts across $940.00 to $985.00, tying a hard structural stop at $857.69, and tracking Oncology margins, Wellverse separation milestones, and IRA Part B policy developments, we ensure that every dollar we eventually commit to McKesson enters with the odds tilted decisively in our favor.

book_subsections.title: Portfolio Fit, Risk Heat, and the Discipline of Waiting
paragraphs: Think about what McKesson adds to our broader U.S. portfolio once it hits our $940.00 to $985.00 buy zone. Today, our combined Schwab and Robinhood book carries heavy exposure to high-beta technology and AI-infrastructure names like Arista Networks, DigitalOcean, Bloom Energy, and Vertiv, pushing portfolio-weighted beta above 2.3x. Healthcare represents barely 2% of the book through a small stake in UnitedHealth Group.

Adding a Tier 1 Core Alpha compounder like McKesson at support brings defensive, non-discretionary prescription cash flows that dampen portfolio volatility without sacrificing 12% to 16% long-term EPS compounding. Yet even the best portfolio diversifier must earn its entry price. By refusing to chase 1W RSI (71.10) at $1,069.43 and keeping 100% cash dry for the $940.00 to $985.00 shelf, we protect our downside today and set up a 1.69:1 asymmetric winner tomorrow.

book_subsections.title: Catalyst Calendar and What We Watch Into FY2028
paragraphs: Between now and our fiscal 2028 fair value horizon, three clear milestones will test our thesis. First, Q3 and Q4 FY2027 earnings updates will show whether Oncology & Multispecialty and Prescription Technology Solutions sustain their margin expansion as Precision Medicine Group integrates [6, 14]. Second, execution milestones on the Wellverse Medical-Surgical separation will confirm how cleanly McKesson releases its higher-multiple pharma and oncology core [9, 10]. Third, federal rulemaking on Medicare Part B negotiation and 340B rebate models will clarify whether policy headwinds stay manageable [4, 20].
With our alerts set at $940.00 to $985.00, our structural stop locked at $857.69, and 100% of earmarked cash ready, we have a complete, repeatable institutional playbook.

Before we lock in our spine and executive summary, remember one final rule of risk management: position sizing is how you survive being wrong. Even a Tier 1 Core Alpha compounder with a 90%+ oligopoly moat can hit an unexpected regulatory air pocket or suffer a broad market de-rating. By sizing the position only inside the $940.00 to $985.00 zone and capping per-share risk at $82.31 to $127.31 against the $857.69 stop, a worst-case stop-out remains a manageable portfolio scratch rather than a permanent impairment of capital. That is how disciplined underwriting protects both your upside and your sleep.

In closing, McKesson's probability-weighted expected value of $1,161.50 (+20.7% from our $962.50 entry midpoint), paired with its Tier 1 Core Alpha durability and 100% cash-ready posture, makes ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP the clearest and most disciplined call we can make.

That alignment across all three time horizons—caution on short-term 1-to-3 month momentum, opportunistic accumulation on 6-to-24 month dips to $940.00–$985.00, and high-conviction 3-to-5 year compounding—is the hallmark of institutional capital allocation. You do not need to predict tomorrow's market bounce to win with McKesson; you only need to set your price alerts, keep your cash dry, and execute without hesitation when the tape delivers your entry zone.

Keep your eyes on three simple numbers over the coming quarters: $940.00 to $985.00 for entry, $857.69 for structural invalidation, and $1,200.00 for base-case fair value. Everything else—daily headlines, macro noise, and short-term market swings—is secondary to that disciplined framework. When a Tier 1 Core Alpha compounder meets an institutional demand shelf, we will be ready to act with full conviction.

Here is your final step-by-step execution checklist before we close the monograph. First, verify that MCK remains NOT_HELD and keep 100% of your earmarked allocation in cash rather than chasing $1,069.43 or substituting Eli Lilly or Cencora. Second, set automated price alerts at $985.00 (the top of our entry zone, just above the rising $974.32 50-day SMA) and at $954.05 (the 20-day swing low). Third, when price enters the $940.00 to $985.00 shelf, confirm that selling volume is drying up and that 4H RSI (currently 51.47) is turning back upward before staging your limit buys. Fourth, attach your hard structural stop-loss at $857.69—safely beneath the 30-week SMA ($870.67) and 200-day SMA ($879.78)—so your downside is strictly capped at 1.69:1 asymmetry against our $1,200.00 base target. Fifth, track Q3 and Q4 FY2027 updates on Oncology margins, Wellverse separation, and IRA Part B rulemaking.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Great investing is knowing what to own and refusing to chase it. McKesson is a Tier 1 Core Alpha compounder, but keeping 100% cash dry until price touches $940–$985 turns a 0.62:1 chase into a 1.69:1 institutional entry.
